content: It describes how these drugs influence each other's levels or effects, primarily through mechanisms such as hepatic or intestinal enzyme metabolism (e.g., CYP3A4, CYP2C19) or transport proteins like P-glycoprotein (MDR1). Below is a professional interpretation of the key points: 1. Clarithromycin and Telavancin: Both drugs can prolong the QTc interval, necessitating caution and close monitoring. 2. Clarithromycin and Teniposide: Clarithromycin increases teniposide levels or effects by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Therapy should be modified or monitored closely. 3. Clarithromycin and Terbinafine: Clarithromycin raises terbinafine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 4. Clarithromycin and Tezacaftor: Clarithromycin increases tezacaftor levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust tezacaftor dosage if co-administered with strong CYP3A inhibitors. 5. Clarithromycin and Thiamine: Clarithromycin decreases thiamine levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. 6. Clarithromycin and Ticagrelor: Clarithromycin increases ticagrelor levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid using ticagrelor with strong CYP3A inhibitors. 7. Clarithromycin and Tinidazole: Clarithromycin raises tinidazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 8. Clarithromycin and Tisotumab Vedotin: Clarithromycin increases tisotumab vedotin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 9. Clarithromycin and Tobramycin: Clarithromycin increases tobramycin levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor. 10. Omeprazole and Tofacitinib: Omeprazole increases tofacitinib levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. No specific dose adjustment is recommended unless co-administered with both moderate CYP3A4 and potent CYP2C19 inhibitors. 11. Clarithromycin and Tolvaptan: Clarithromycin increases tolvaptan levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor. 12. Clarithromycin and Tramadol: Clarithromycin raises tramadol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 13. Clarithromycin and Trimethoprim: Both drugs can prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or monitored closely. 14. Clarithromycin and Trimipramine: Clarithromycin increases trimipramine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 15. Clarithromycin and Triptorelin: Triptorelin increases clarithromycin toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval, raising the risk of torsades de pointes. Use caution and monitor. 16. Clarithromycin and Tropisetron: Both drugs can prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or monitored closely. 17. Clarithromycin and Ulipristal: Clarithromycin increases ulipristal levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 18. Clarithromycin and Umeclidinium Bromide/Vilanterol: Clarithromycin raises levels of these inhaled agents by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or monitored closely. 19. Clarithromycin and Upadacitinib: Clarithromycin increases upadacitinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution if co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 20. Clarithromycin and Valbenazine: Clarithromycin increases valbenazine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs can prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or monitored closely. 21. Clarithromycin and Valsartan: Clarithromycin increases valsartan levels by inhibiting hepatic uptake transporters (OATP1B1). Use caution and monitor. 22. Clarithromycin and Vamorolone: Clarithromycin raises vamorolone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the starting dose of vamorolone to 4 mg/kg/day, not exceeding 200 mg/day for patients weighing over 50 kg. 23. Clarithromycin and Vardenafil: Clarithromycin increases vardenafil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or monitored closely. 24. Clarithromycin and Velpatasvir: Clarithromycin raises velpatasvir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 25. Clarithromycin and Venlafaxine: Both drugs can prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or monitored closely. 26. Clarithromycin and Verapamil: Clarithromycin increases verapamil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This may lead to hypotension, edema, bradycardia, and acute kidney injury due to reduced renal blood flow. Use caution and monitor. 27. Clarithromycin and Vinblastine: Clarithromycin raises vinblastine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor. 28. Clarithromycin and Vincristine: Clarithromycin increases vincristine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor. 29. Clarithromycin and Vincristine Liposomal: Clarithromycin raises vincristine liposomal levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor. 30. Clarithromycin and Vinorelbine: Clarithromycin increases vinorelbine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 31. Omeprazole and Vismodegib: Omeprazole decreases vismodegib levels by increasing gastric pH, potentially reducing its bioavailability. The effect on efficacy is unknown. Use caution and monitor. 32. Clarithromycin and Zidovudine: Clarithromycin increases zidovudine toxicity through an unknown mechanism. Separate administration by at least 2 to 4 hours. 33. Clarithromycin and Ziprasidone: Clarithromycin raises ziprasidone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 34. Clarithromycin and Zonisamide: Clarithromycin increases zonisamide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 35. Clarithromycin and Zuranolone: Clarithromycin raises zuranolone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the zuranolone dose if co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. This list highlights the importance of monitoring and adjusting therapy when clarithromycin or omeprazole is co-administered with other medications, particularly those metabolized by CYP enzymes or transported by P-glycoprotein.
